resources.why: Shows why margin includes historical/stress risk, liquidity and concentration. Useful for funding-risk reasoning; product rollout and broker requirements are separate checks.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Euan Sinclair — Volatility Trading, 2nd edition

resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Jim Gatheral — The Volatility Surface: A Practitioner’s Guide
resources.why: A focused bridge between smiles, local/stochastic volatility and model behavior. Requires calculus and pricing foundations.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Demeterfi, Derman, Kamal and Zou — More Than You Ever Wanted to Know About Volatility Swaps
resources.why: Foundational replication logic for variance/volatility swaps. Explicitly examine continuous-path assumptions, strike truncation and jump limitations.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: MIT OCW — Finance Theory I
resources.why: Provides present value, fixed income, equities, derivatives and portfolio theory with problem sets. The course is historical; institutional details need current sources.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: SEC — Beginners’ Guide to Financial Statements
resources.why: A free accounting entry point for understanding the underlying business before studying equity-event risk.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: St. Louis Fed — ALFRED and real-time periods
resources.why: Explains historical data vintages, which are essential for macro backtests that use only information available at the time.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.why: Separates variance expectations from the variance premium. Useful for challenging the idea that VIX is simply a physical-probability volatility forecast.

resources.title: MIT OCW — Introduction to Probability and Statistics, 18.05

resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: James, Witten, Hastie, Tibshirani and Taylor — An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python
resources.why: Strong supervised/unsupervised learning foundations with practical labs. Financial time dependence requires additional validation controls beyond generic examples.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado and Zhu — The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
resources.why: Makes strategy-selection risk explicit. Study assumptions and limitations rather than treating a diagnostic as certification that an edge exists.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Steven Shreve — Stochastic Calculus for Finance II
resources.why: The continuous-time mathematical track: Brownian motion, Ito calculus, pricing measures and derivative valuation. Use Volume I first for discrete-time foundations if needed.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: MIT OCW — Analytics of Finance
resources.why: Graduate material and exercises connecting stochastic calculus, pricing and financial analytics. A structured complement to textbook derivations.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: IRS — Publication 550
resources.why: U.S. options, straddles and Section 1256 treatment. Classification depends on instrument and circumstances; use the tax-year version and applicable professional advice.

resources.title: John J. Murphy — Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
resources.why: Broad vocabulary for charts, trends, indicators and intermarket analysis. Use as a taxonomy, paired with empirical testing; popularity and visual examples do not prove profitability.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Steve Nison — Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques
resources.why: Useful for precise candlestick names and contextual interpretation. Cap memorization effort and test objective definitions against base rates and costs.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Lo, Mamaysky and Wang — Foundations of Technical Analysis
resources.why: Shows how subjective pattern claims can become statistical tests. Incremental information in a historical sample is not proof that every pattern yields net tradable profits.
resources.access: Abstract and publication metadata checked; paper studies U.S. stock data from 1962–1996, not all instruments or current markets.

resources.title: Cboe — Complex Order Handling
resources.why: Grounds package execution in actual order-book and auction mechanisms. Venue details and admissible ratios must be checked for the chosen exchange.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: OCC — Information Memos
resources.why: The primary lookup for adjusted contracts, expiration handling and corporate actions. Search the exact contract and effective date rather than relying on a generic multiplier.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Cboe — 0DTEs Decoded: Positioning, Trends, and Market Impact
resources.why: A data-based counterweight to gross-volume dealer-gamma narratives. The exchange is commercially interested, and its sample and methodology do not settle every market-impact question.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: QuantLib — Official Documentation
resources.why: A reference implementation ecosystem for calendars, curves, instruments and numerical pricing. Validate conventions and outputs rather than treating library results as unquestionable.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Robert Engle — Risk and Volatility: Econometric Models and Financial Practice
resources.why: An authoritative introduction to conditional volatility modeling and its economic purpose; a starting point for GARCH and volatility forecasting.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Gatheral and Jacquier — Arbitrage-free SVI Volatility Surfaces

resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Cboe — VIX FAQ

resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Cboe — Index Governance and Volatility Methodologies
resources.why: Primary methodology directory for volatility indices. Use the exact index version, calculation rules, eligibility and change notices.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Cboe — Options on VIX Futures
resources.why: Prevents conflation with cash-settled VIX index options: the product page describes options delivering into VIX futures.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Steven Heston — A Closed-Form Solution for Options with Stochastic Volatility
resources.why: The 1993 stochastic-volatility model connects spot/variance correlation, smile and characteristic-function pricing. Validate calibration and hedges, not just price fit.

resources.title: Hagan, Kumar, Lesniewski and Woodward — Managing Smile Risk

resources.title: Gatheral, Jaisson and Rosenbaum — Volatility Is Rough
resources.why: A research-frontier extension linking volatility regularity, estimation and forecasting. Include competing evidence and microstructure/estimation limitations before adoption.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: CFTC — Interim Report on WTI Trading Around April 20, 2020
resources.why: A concrete case for delivery constraints, negative prices and model assumptions. The report itself does not claim a complete causal account of every price movement.

resources.title: ESMA — EMIR Article 41: Margin Requirements

resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: McNeil, Frey and Embrechts — Quantitative Risk Management
resources.why: Systematic treatment of loss distributions, risk measures, dependence and aggregation. Valuable for understanding why normal-distribution shortcuts fail in option books.
resources.access: Publisher catalog entry checked; book landing page blocked to this research tool. Full book was not read in this session.

resources.title: Federal Reserve — SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management
resources.why: A current institutional model-governance reference for development, validation and controls. Adapt the principles to scale; banking guidance is not a retail-trader legal obligation.
resources.access: April 17, 2026 official letter checked; it supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8.

resources.title: Eurex — Clearing Prisma
resources.why: A second clearing framework for comparing liquidation groups, portfolio margin and stress concepts with CME methods.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: SEC — Knight Capital Market Access Rule Enforcement
resources.why: Demonstrates how deployment failures, missing controls and ignored warnings can overwhelm a trading business. Use for incident reconstruction and control design.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: FINRA — Business Continuity Planning
resources.why: Useful for identifying critical systems, counterparties and recovery processes. Distinguish institutional obligations from sensible controls for an individual.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Avellaneda and Stoikov — High-frequency Trading in a Limit Order Book

resources.access: Author’s university publication listing checked; follow its original-paper link.

resources.access: Original Journal of Risk publisher record checked; full publisher text may be paywalled.

resources.title: Wharton WRDS — OptionMetrics
resources.why: Illustrates the data fields and corporate-action histories professional option research needs. Dataset availability, licensing and vendor modeling assumptions must be evaluated.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Python — Official Tutorial
resources.why: A reliable language foundation before financial scripting. Learn functions, errors, modules and data structures before broker automation.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Bailey and López de Prado — The Deflated Sharpe Ratio
resources.why: Addresses selection bias and non-normal returns in reported performance. Useful alongside transparent trial counts and true holdouts; not an edge guarantee.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen — Time Series Momentum, original paper data
resources.why: A reproducible starting point for trend evidence across futures markets. Does not validate arbitrary technical indicators, option implementations or every future regime.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: pandas — User Guide
resources.why: Supports correct joins, time series, missing-data handling and reproducible analytics; financial semantics and point-in-time alignment remain the researcher’s responsibility.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: SEBI — Individual Equity-Derivatives Trading Behaviour, FY25–FY26
resources.why: Use alongside the FY22–FY24 study to investigate trader outcomes, costs and behavior. Compare study definitions and populations; do not turn an aggregate loss rate into an individual forecast.

resources.title: NSE — Equity Derivatives Contract Information
resources.why: Primary entry point for specifications, permitted lots, underlying lists and quantity freezes. Capture effective dates and the actual daily contract master.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: NSE — Securities Transaction Tax
resources.why: Shows the need to distinguish transaction type and taxable base. Recheck current rates and law for the trade date rather than retaining a remembered percentage.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.why: Use the applicable law, year, definitions and transition provisions for Indian derivatives. Older section numbers and summaries cannot be assumed to apply unchanged.
resources.access: Official legislation located and relevant definitions surfaced; this curriculum does not make a personalized tax determination.

resources.title: FINRA — Rule 4210: Margin Requirements
resources.why: Primary rule source for U.S. securities margin. Check amendments, implementation dates, exchange rules and broker overlays instead of repeating historic thresholds.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: CFTC — Basics of Futures Trading
resources.why: Establishes futures mechanics and the distinct regulatory setting; follow current contract and intermediary rules for operational decisions.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: HKEX — Hang Seng Index Options
resources.why: A concrete non-U.S. specification exercise: compare multiplier, sessions, exercise and settlement instead of generalizing from another market.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Barber and Odean — Trading Is Hazardous to Your Wealth
resources.why: Links trading frequency and net household performance in its studied sample. Use to study costs and behavior; distinguish stock investors from all options traders.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.why: Useful for deliberate practice, review and niche-specific skill development. Separate coaching methods and anecdotes from controlled evidence of improved trading returns.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: Federal Reserve — Hedge Funds, Leverage and the Lessons of LTCM
resources.why: A primary historical account for excessive leverage, counterparty discipline and funding constraints in relative-value strategies.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: SEC — Equity and Options Market Structure Conditions in Early 2021
resources.why: Use to compare evidence on equity and options flows against single-cause squeeze narratives; separate observations from causal inference.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.title: FCA — UK EMIR
resources.why: A current entry point for UK derivatives reporting, clearing and risk-mitigation scope. Contrast with EU rules and actual participant classification.
resources.access: Official page, abstract or publisher contents checked; full text may require separate study.

resources.why: The discrete-time derivation makes replication and American exercise accessible before continuous-time mathematics.

M01.exercise: Build a cash-flow and return ledger with fees, financing and a drawdown/recovery sequence.
M01.mastery: Reconcile cash, equity and net return without confusing notional with money at risk.

M02.exercise: Compare a stock, ETF, leveraged ETF, future, option and swap expressing a similar thesis.
M02.mastery: Identify ownership, leverage, path dependence, counterparty and settlement differences.

M03.exercise: Trace a simulated trade from order to custody and settlement, including a holiday and corporate action.
M03.mastery: Identify who owes what to whom and when, including a failed-settlement contingency.

M04.exercise: Replay market, limit, stop and stop-limit orders through a gapping order book.
M04.mastery: Explain fills, non-fills, partial fills and why a stop does not guarantee an exit price.

M05.exercise: Calculate net expectancy with commissions, spread, financing, borrow and turnover.
M05.mastery: Reject a gross-profitable strategy when plausible costs or funding make it uneconomic.

M06.exercise: Read one company filing and produce a one-page earnings-risk brief.
M06.mastery: Separate reported facts, adjusted measures, expectations and unsupported narrative.

M07.exercise: Reconstruct an economic release using the first release and later revisions.
M07.mastery: Distinguish what was knowable at the decision time from hindsight.

M08.exercise: Estimate rolling equity/bond/dollar/volatility relationships in calm and stressed samples.
M08.mastery: Explain why a single correlation estimate is not a stable hedge guarantee.

M09.exercise: Build a timestamped calendar and outcome tree for overlapping company and macro events.
M09.mastery: Identify gaps, rescheduling, release-time uncertainty and conditional outcomes.

M10.exercise: Solve conditional-probability, expectancy, skewed-payoff and probability-of-touch problems.
M10.mastery: Distinguish frequency, belief, pricing probability and payoff-weighted expectation.

M11.exercise: Estimate an edge with uncertainty, then repeat after multiple-testing correction.
M11.mastery: Explain effect size, sample dependence, power and why a small p-value is insufficient.

M12.exercise: Compare random-walk, simple volatility and more complex forecasts on rolling holdouts.
M12.mastery: Show that any improvement survives correct timing and a simple benchmark.

M13.exercise: Check analytic derivatives against finite differences and solve an IV-style root problem.
M13.mastery: Explain units, tolerance, conditioning and convergence failure.

M14.exercise: Derive a self-financing diffusion hedge and simulate Brownian/GBM paths.
M14.mastery: Use Ito's second-order term correctly and distinguish physical from pricing drift.

M15.exercise: Annotate unseen charts with a frozen rule for swings, regimes and invalidation.
M15.mastery: Produce consistent labels without using future bars or inventing participant intent.

M16.exercise: Label randomized candle examples before seeing subsequent prices.
M16.mastery: State context, alternative outcomes and an objective rule for each studied formation.

M17.exercise: Operationalize one chart pattern and compare outcomes with matched non-pattern controls.
M17.mastery: Report failures and base rates; do not select examples only after favorable outcomes.

M18.exercise: Implement several trend indicators and compare lag, turnover and signal correlation.
M18.mastery: Identify redundant filters and demonstrate sensitivity to lookback choices.

M19.exercise: Test RSI/MACD or another momentum pair across trending and ranging samples.
M19.mastery: Avoid equating thresholds with universal reversal signals.

M20.exercise: Reconcile VWAP/profile calculations and compare ATR with realized-return volatility.
M20.mastery: Explain different units, feed coverage, anchor choices and non-equivalent measures.

M21.exercise: Decode unfamiliar live or archived contract specifications and construct basic payoff tables.
M21.mastery: Get underlying, multiplier, units, exercise style and settlement correct on every case.

M22.exercise: Work through early assignment, an ex-dividend date, a near-strike expiry and a one-leg exercise.
M22.mastery: Produce correct resulting positions, deadlines and cash/share obligations.

M23.exercise: Audit a timestamped chain containing stale quotes, large OI and an ambiguous block trade.
M23.mastery: Separate observed information from inferred direction, dealer inventory and probability.

M24.exercise: Complete the strategy dossier for each single-leg or stock-linked construction.
M24.mastery: Rebuild signed legs and exposures from first principles without relying on the name.

M25.exercise: Derive all four verticals and reconcile equivalent debit/credit terminal payoffs.
M25.mastery: Calculate bounds and explain how expiry operations can create additional exposure.

M26.exercise: Construct long/short volatility structures and compare spot/IV/time scenarios.
M26.mastery: Identify where net Greeks change sign and where high win rates hide severe losses.

M27.exercise: Value calendars, diagonals and ratios before and at the front expiry.
M27.mastery: Avoid assigning a model-free single-expiry maximum profit to a multi-expiry position.

M28.exercise: Build a conversion, reversal and European box with full dated cash flows.
M28.mastery: Separate replication identity from implementable profit after borrow, financing and exercise.

M29.exercise: Derive forward pricing and parity, then test executable quotes against valid bounds.
M29.mastery: State every contract/carry assumption and diagnose apparent arbitrage from bad data.

M30.exercise: Build a binomial tree, compare with BSM, and price an American exercise case.
M30.mastery: Explain convergence, early-exercise economics and when the selected model is unsuitable.

M31.exercise: Price a benchmark with two numerical methods and publish convergence/error plots.
M31.mastery: Reconcile results within justified tolerances and explain residual error.

M32.exercise: Calculate per-contract and portfolio Greeks under spot/time/IV shifts.
M32.mastery: Keep units and signs consistent and distinguish delta from actual profit probability.

M33.exercise: Verify selected higher-order Greeks numerically under stated time and volatility units.
M33.mastery: Explain nonstandard names, cross terms and why local sensitivities fail in large shocks.

M34.exercise: Replay delta hedging with two hedge frequencies and a jump scenario.
M34.mastery: Reconcile hedge cash flows, option P&L, theta, fees and unexplained residuals.

M35.exercise: Compare realized-volatility estimators with gaps and high-frequency noise.
M35.mastery: Choose an estimator appropriate to the forecast target and report uncertainty.

M36.exercise: Compare trailing realized volatility, forecast variance, IV rank and an implied distribution.
M36.mastery: Explain why historical ranking alone cannot establish that an option is cheap.

M37.exercise: Build a small synchronized surface and check strike/calendar consistency.
M37.mastery: Report forward inputs, conventions, bid/ask uncertainty and failed arbitrage checks.

M38.exercise: Estimate an event contribution using expiries around an announcement.
M38.mastery: State baseline assumptions and evaluate direction, jump asymmetry and post-event repricing.

M39.exercise: Compare VIX, a VIX future, VIX index option and option on a VIX future.
M39.mastery: Identify exposure, settlement and why an ETP need not track changes in spot VIX.

M40.exercise: Calibrate two models and compare fit, parameter stability and hedge behavior.
M40.mastery: Explain tradeoffs; do not equate lower calibration error with a superior trading model.

M41.exercise: Produce a volatility-relative-value proposal with hedge policy and stress scenarios.
M41.mastery: Identify all residual directional, jump, correlation, funding and model exposures.

M42.exercise: Trace a futures roll and an exercised futures option through margin and settlement.
M42.mastery: Distinguish spot return, roll, collateral return and physical delivery obligations.

M43.exercise: Compare equivalent-seeming equity, FX, rates and commodity option quotations.
M43.mastery: Convert units and explain discounting, collateral and settlement differences.

M44.exercise: Decompose an exotic/structured product and read a sample term sheet.
M44.mastery: Identify path dependence, exercise, model, counterparty and documentation risks.

M45.exercise: Size a skewed-payoff position under several edge and loss assumptions.
M45.mastery: Keep loss/cash needs within a declared budget and reject infeasible minimum contract sizes.

M46.exercise: Stress an option book with joint spot, skew, volatility, liquidity and margin shocks.
M46.mastery: Identify ruin paths and funding failure even when final terminal payoff seems acceptable.

M47.exercise: Create a dated cash/collateral ladder including assignment and stressed margin.
M47.mastery: Show how all obligations could be met without assuming instant transfers or liquid markets.

M48.exercise: Aggregate a portfolio of superficially different option strategies.
M48.mastery: Expose shared beta/short-volatility risks and propose measurable concentration limits.

M49.exercise: Run a tabletop outage, duplicate-order and stale-data incident.
M49.mastery: Contain new risk, reconcile positions and restore operation using a documented procedure.

M50.exercise: Analyze a quote/trade replay for spread, depth, queue position and price discovery.
M50.mastery: Separate observed facts, model assumptions and plausible alternative explanations.

M51.exercise: Build dealer-gamma estimates under opposing inventory-sign assumptions.
M51.mastery: Report a sensitivity range and demonstrate why OI alone does not reveal the actual book.

M52.exercise: Compare package execution policies on identical opportunities.
M52.mastery: Attribute fill quality, non-fill cost, adverse selection and net implementation shortfall.

M53.exercise: Compare hold, close and roll policies using the same starting trade and prices.
M53.mastery: Count every cash flow and evaluate the new exposure independently of sunk loss.

M54.exercise: Build a small point-in-time options dataset with corporate actions and missing quotes.
M54.mastery: Produce an auditable data dictionary, exclusion log and timestamp checks.

M55.exercise: Write a preregistered hypothesis and attempt to falsify it.
M55.mastery: Document rationale, null, tests, search count, costs and rejection criteria before results.

M56.exercise: Run an options backtest including expiry, capital and realistic execution.
M56.mastery: Reproduce a hand-calculated sample and preserve a genuinely untouched holdout.

M57.exercise: Compare a simple forecasting rule with a statistical-learning model.
M57.mastery: Show incremental out-of-sample benefit or correctly reject the added complexity.

M58.exercise: Build a paper-only analytics pipeline from ingestion to positions and risk.
M58.mastery: Independently verify numbers and recover from a dropped message or rejected order.

M59.exercise: Write a complete one-market trading-system specification.
M59.mastery: Another person must be able to reproduce every decision and identify when trading is prohibited.

M60.exercise: Keep a forecast/decision journal and replay a winning and losing streak.
M60.mastery: Identify behavior changes, follow pause rules and judge decisions from ex-ante information.

M61.exercise: Analyze a full journal including fees, adjustments, missed trades and withdrawals.
M61.mastery: Reconcile totals and separate exposure, execution, process and statistical uncertainty.

M62.exercise: Complete a dated U.S. instrument/account/rules worksheet.
M62.mastery: Locate current official rules and broker cutoffs; explain where instrument-specific tax advice is needed.

M63.exercise: Complete a dated Indian contract, fee, margin, delivery and tax worksheet.
M63.mastery: Verify live listings and effective dates; never fill current lots or tax rates from memory.

M64.exercise: Compare the same intended exposure in two jurisdictions.
M64.mastery: Identify access, settlement, collateral, currency, reporting and tax differences.

M65.exercise: Write an evidence verdict for each listed myth with a counterexample or test design.
M65.mastery: Distinguish false, overstated, unsupported and context-dependent claims without replacing one myth with another.

M66.exercise: Reconstruct a documented loss event and map each failure to a control.
M66.mastery: Distinguish known facts from hindsight and show which losses the control could realistically prevent.

M67.exercise: Present a desk-style proposal, daily risk report and incident response to a skeptical reviewer.
M67.mastery: Defend assumptions, admit unknowns, reconcile numbers and comply with a written mandate.

stages.title: Financial orientation
stages.gate: Reconcile money, returns, leverage and objectives. Introduce the safety briefing and journal immediately.

stages.title: How markets and accounts work
stages.gate: Trace a trade, choose orders and calculate realistic costs/cash needs.

stages.title: Probability, statistics and core mathematics
stages.gate: Solve uncertain-payoff problems; learn algebra/calculus entry skills. Defer specialist numerical/PDE extensions.

stages.title: Underlying, macro, events and time series
stages.gate: Separate information, expectation and hindsight; build elementary forecasts.

stages.title: Price behavior and technical-analysis literacy
stages.gate: Label unseen data and test one chosen method; keep most named patterns/indicators as reference material.

stages.title: Options and local-market operations
stages.gate: Decode contracts and pass exercise/settlement cases. Complete the selected jurisdiction branch; survey others.

stages.title: Pricing and primary Greeks
stages.gate: Derive replication/parity/binomial logic and calculate risk in correct units. Defer full stochastic derivations.

stages.title: Realized and implied volatility
stages.gate: Match forecasts to priced risks; distinguish IV ranking, expectation and risk premium.

stages.title: Risk, funding, operational control and behavior
stages.gate: Pass sizing, stress, cash-obligation and error-containment gates before implementing strategies.

stages.title: Strategy construction and surface literacy
stages.gate: Complete signed-leg dossiers; learn surface/term structure before multi-expiry valuation.

stages.title: Execution and position management
stages.gate: Reconcile fills and evaluate hold/close/adjust/roll policies with all cash flows.

stages.title: Research, software, systems and performance
stages.gate: Build a reproducible study, honest backtest, written system and complete journal analysis. Python basics can be introduced earlier.

stages.title: Dynamic hedging, futures and portfolio risk
stages.gate: Explain hedged P&L, distinguish futures/VIX products and stress a portfolio.

stages.title: Advanced trading and empirical specialization
stages.gate: Defend relative-value, dealer-flow and systematic-model hypotheses under realistic costs and alternative explanations.

stages.title: Professional quantitative models
stages.gate: Complete stochastic-calculus derivations, numerical validation and surface/model calibration for a quant track.

stages.title: Cross-asset, exotic and OTC specialist branches
stages.gate: Master the conventions and model/legal risks relevant to the selected product mandate.

stages.title: Failure analysis and professional integration
stages.gate: Pass integrated capstones, incident drills and a skeptical review of a desk-style mandate.
